Persistent previews of complete tables

Source: R/preview.R
special-print.Rd

preview_table() keeps the complete data and remembers how to print it. The default shows the first five and last five rows. Interval previews show evenly spaced rows. unpreview_table() removes the preference.

print_headtail() and print_interval() print once and invisibly return the unchanged input. print_all() prints every row and every column, like Stata's list, and also returns the input invisibly. s_print() does all three through one style argument. slice_headtail() and slice_interval() actually select rows, so use them only when a smaller data set is wanted.

Usage

preview_table(.data, style = c("headtail", "interval"), n = 10)

unpreview_table(.data)

print_headtail(
  .data,
  n = 10,
  width = NULL,
  ...,
  max_extra_cols = NULL,
  max_footer_lines = NULL
)

s_print(
  .data,
  style = c("headtail", "interval", "all"),
  n = 10,
  width = NULL,
  ...
)

print_all(.data, ...)

print_interval(
  .data,
  n = 10,
  width = NULL,
  ...,
  max_extra_cols = NULL,
  max_footer_lines = NULL
)

slice_headtail(.data, n = 10)

slice_interval(.data, n = 10)

Arguments

.data

An in-memory data frame, data.table, ordinary tibble, grouped tibble, rowwise tibble, or sf data frame (geometry is kept when slicing and printed as a column). Convert other subclasses explicitly before wrapping; collect lazy tables first. Apply the wrapper separately to lists of tables.

style

Either "headtail" or "interval". s_print() also accepts "all", which prints every row and column like print_all().

n

Total number of rows to display or select: a positive whole number or Inf for all rows. An odd head/tail budget gives the head the extra row. With n = 1, both styles select the first row. Short tables never repeat rows.

width

Console width, passed to tibble formatting. NULL uses the current console width; Inf shows all columns.

...

Additional arguments passed to tibble formatting.

max_extra_cols, max_footer_lines

Tibble formatting controls.

Value

preview_table() returns the complete input container with an additional tidystata_preview class. unpreview_table() returns the table without that class or its settings, preserving grouping. The print helpers invisibly return their original input. The slice helpers return the selected rows in the input container, retaining valid grouping and existing preview settings. Explicit base data.frame row names are preserved. Slice helpers regenerate automatic row names following dplyr's row-slicing behavior. Other subclasses are unsupported.

Details

Preview settings survive table subsetting/replacement, dplyr mutation, filtering, sorting, column selection, renaming, relocation, distinct rows, slicing, grouping, rowwise operations, summaries and reframing, as well as tidyr's pivot_longer() and pivot_wider(). Grouping follows the underlying operation. Joins inherit the left input's settings; bind_rows() inherits the first input's settings. Arbitrary third-party transformations and direct vctrs::vec_rbind() are not covered by this guarantee.

Positions shown in the margin refer to the current table, not the original data before filtering or sorting. Previewing does not change column values, classes, labels, or the data used in subsequent calculations. Grouped tables use a global row budget, not a separate budget per group.

print(x, n = Inf) displays the entire table. Per-call formatting overrides do not change stored settings. Explicit tibble::as_tibble() or as.data.frame() conversions remove the preview, as does extracting a column. This feature controls console printing, not HTML widgets or GUI viewers. Only the temporary display is converted to a tibble. Wrapping and unwrapping a data.table creates an independent copy; native operations such as := on a wrapped data.table retain ordinary reference semantics. External dplyr/tidyr verbs determine their own result container and grouping, while preview settings follow the result.

See also

Other selection and preview functions: s_select(), varlist()

Examples

x <- preview_table(tibble::tibble(id = 1:30, value = (1:30)^2))
x
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  2     2     4
#>  3     3     9
#>  4     4    16
#>  5     5    25
#> 26    26   676
#> 27    27   729
#> 28    28   784
#> 29    29   841
#> 30    30   900
#> # ... 20 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.
dplyr::filter(x, id > 10)
#> # A tibble: 20 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1    11   121
#>  2    12   144
#>  3    13   169
#>  4    14   196
#>  5    15   225
#> 16    26   676
#> 17    27   729
#> 18    28   784
#> 19    29   841
#> 20    30   900
#> # ... 10 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.
preview_table(x, style = "interval", n = 5)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  8     8    64
#> 16    16   256
#> 23    23   529
#> 30    30   900
#> # ... 25 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to
#> # show all rows.
print(x, n = Inf)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1

unpreview_table(x)

#>    <int> <dbl>
